message.content: {"winner":"A","evidence_A":"About 140 words, close to the target. Formal abstract tone. Covers the problem, the ESO ToO method, the consortium and LP, and milestones, and states nine activations with three OTs. Minor issues: it says 'since 2000' instead of 'up to Dec 2000', and it presents short GRBs as ongoing work although the body lists them only as an LP aim. Findings are listed generically.","evidence_B":"About 170 words, an overshoot of roughly 25%. Uses an informal second-person register ('you got'), which is unsuitable for an abstract. Omits LP results such as the nine activations. Claims the Italian-Dutch pair 'brought in' the other nodes, which oversimplifies the body. The rotation description ignores the later 15-day rule and the sixth node.","comparative_reason":"A is better on all three criteria. It has appropriate abstract style, broader coverage including the LP outcomes, and near-target length. B's casual voice, overshoot, and omission of LP findings weaken it substantially."}
